title: Thalamus-to-visual-cortex spike links in two Allen mouse Neuropixels data sets increase with tracer axon density only weakly; LP gives fewer links to V1 than to higher areas
abstract: Question: does mesoscale tracer axon density predict how often thalamic and visual-cortex units show fast directed spike links? Data: Allen Visual Coding Neuropixels (46 mice, 1,049,307 thalamus-cortex pairs) and Visual Behavior Neuropixels (69 mice, 768,943 pairs); LGd and LP units against units in six visual areas (V1, LM, RL, AL, PM, AM). A link is a cross-correlogram peak at +1 to +4 ms (thalamus leads) or -4 to -1 ms (cortex leads) above a hollow-Gaussian baseline. Anatomy: Allen tracer experiments; because many LP and LGd injections label both nuclei, the primary estimate used clean injections only. Result 1 (pre-specified, passed): with nucleus and area fixed effects, spike-count and cell-class controls, the odds of a thalamus-leading link increased 2.59 times (95% CI 1.58-4.24) and 1.92 times (1.47-2.52) per 10-fold density; route permutation p = 0.045 and 0.0013. Unmixed and all-injection tracer estimates, a sharp baseline, strict thresholds and different-probe pairs gave the same sign. The relation is compressed: density spans about 900-fold across the 12 routes, link rates about 10-fold. In Visual Coding a control lag (+21 to +24 ms) also had a slope (1.66), and the slope depended on the LGd-to-V1 route. Exploratory: LP projects more densely to V1 than to higher areas, but LP-to-V1 pairs had fewer links (odds ratio 0.49, 0.34-0.71; Visual Behavior 0.77, 0.53-1.10); LP-to-V1 axons end mostly in layers 1 and 5. LGd links preferred V1 only 2.6-4 times, against a 150-fold density ratio. Result 2 (pre-specified, failed): cortex-leading links did not follow area-to-thalamus density (1.40 and 1.14 per 10-fold, CIs include 1), stayed near control-lag rates, and came more from fast-spiking units, which do not project to the thalamus. Limitations: CCG links are putative; 12 routes give few degrees of freedom; tracer data come from other mice and few clean injections. Allen data are not bundled; code regenerates all derived tables.

display.caption: Percentage of unit pairs with a fast directed spike link against Allen tracer axon density, for each thalamic nucleus (LGd blue circles, LP orange squares) and visual area, in Visual Coding (left) and Visual Behavior (right). Top: thalamus leads (+1 to +4 ms), clean-injection density from nucleus to area. Bottom: cortex leads (-4 to -1 ms), density from area to nucleus. Bars: 95% CI from a bootstrap over mice. Open markers: the same test at a control lag (+21 to +24 ms).

Odds ratio of a link per 10-fold tracer density (95% CI, clustered by mouse) for the primary two-way fixed-effects model and all variants, in Visual Coding (blue circles) and Visual Behavior (green diamonds). Rows after 'Pairs on different probes' are exploratory, except the control-lag and cortex-leading rows.

Pooled cross-correlograms (excess over the hollow-Gaussian baseline) of the detected thalamus-leading links for each route, Visual Coding (dark) and Visual Behavior (light). Shaded: the +1 to +4 ms test window. LP-to-LM, RL and AL links in Visual Coding have a sharp 1.5-2.5 ms peak.
